sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Chemical Reaction (रासायनिक अभिक्रिया)** is a process where reactants are converted into products with new chemical properties.
Occurs whenever bonds between reactant atoms are broken and new bonds are formed under specific conditions (heat, light, catalyst).
Observed everywhere in nature, industrial processes, laboratories, and biological systems (e.g., digestion, respiration).
**Antoine Lavoisier** (Father of Modern Chemistry) established the foundational **Law of Conservation of Mass**.
Crucial for understanding material transformations, energy changes, metallurgy, pharmacology, and industrial manufacturing.
Involves **change in state**, **change in color**, **evolution of gas**, **change in temperature**, and **formation of precipitate**.
High-yield topic in **General Science**, frequently tested through direct questions on **Balancing Equation**, **Oxidation**, **Reduction**, **Acid**, **Base**, **Salt**, and **pH**.
Governed strictly by the **Law of Conservation of Mass** and **Law of Constant Proportions**.

items.title: Types of Chemical Reactions
items.content:
• **Combination Reaction:** Two or more reactants combine to form a single product ($A + B \rightarrow AB$).
• **Decomposition Reaction:** A single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler products ($AB \rightarrow A + B$).
• **Displacement Reaction:** A more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound ($A + BC \rightarrow AC + B$).
• **Double Displacement Reaction:** Exchange of ions between two reactants occurs ($AB + CD \rightarrow AD + CB$).
• **Mnemonic for Reaction Types:** **C**an **D**ogs **D**ance **D**uring **R**ain? (**C**ombination, **D**ecomposition, **D**isplacement, **D**ouble displacement, **R**edox).

items.title: Oxidation and Reduction (Redox Reactions)
items.content:
• **Oxidation:** Addition of **oxygen/non-metallic element** or removal of **hydrogen/metallic element**; loss of electrons.
• **Reduction:** Addition of **hydrogen/metallic element** or removal of **oxygen/non-metallic element**; gain of electrons.
• **Oxidizing Agent:** The substance that gets reduced itself but oxidizes other substances.
• **Reducing Agent:** The substance that gets oxidized itself but reduces other substances.
• **Mnemonic for Oxidation/Reduction:** **OIL RIG** (**O**xidation **I**s **L**oss of electrons, **R**eduction **I**s **G**ain of electrons) and **LEO says GER** (**L**ose **E**lectrons **O**xidation, **G**ain **E**lectrons **R**eduction).

items.title: Acids, Bases, and Salts
items.content:
• **Acids:** Substances that release **$H^+$ ions** in aqueous solution; turn blue litmus **red**; pH less than 7.
• **Bases:** Substances that release **$OH^-$ ions** in aqueous solution; turn red litmus **blue**; pH greater than 7.
• **Salts:** Ionic compounds formed by the neutralization reaction between an acid and a base ($Acid + Base \rightarrow Salt + Water$).
• **Mnemonic for Litmus Paper:** **BAR** (**B**ase turns **A**lkaline/Blue, **R**ed turns blue) or **ANAB** (**A**cid turns **N**eutral/Blue **A**lkaline... wait, use **BRB**: **B**ase **R**ed to **B**lue, and **ARB**: **A**cid **R**ed to **B**lue is incorrect -> **ABR**: **A**cid turns **B**lue to **R**ed).

items.title: pH Scale and Indicators
items.content:
• **pH Scale:** A logarithmic scale from **0 to 14** used to specify the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution.
• **Neutral Point:** pH value of exactly **7** at $25^\circ C$ (pure water).
• **Acidic Range:** pH less than 7 (lower the pH, stronger the acid).
• **Basic Range:** pH greater than 7 (higher the pH, stronger the base).
• **Indicators:** Substances that change color in acidic or basic mediums (e.g., **Phenolphthalein**, **Methyl Orange**, **Turmeric**).

items.title: Balancing Chemical Equations
items.content:
• **Principle:** Based on the **Law of Conservation of Mass** (total mass of reactants equals total mass of products).
• **Method:** Hit and trial method; balancing the atom with the maximum number first.
• **Requirement:** Number of atoms of each element must be equal on both reactant and product sides.
• **Physical States:** Represented using symbols like **(s)** for solid, **(l)** for liquid, **(g)** for gas, and **(aq)** for aqueous.

items.definition: Remember **BRB** for Base (**B**ase turns **R**ed to **B**lue) and consequently **ARB** for Acid (**A**cid turns **B**lue to **R**ed).
Remember **OIL RIG** — **O**xidation **I**s **L**oss (of electrons), **R**eduction **I**s **G**ain (of electrons).
Remember **0 is Acidic (Battery acid/Zero tolerance)**, **7 is Heaven (Neutral/Pure water)**, **14 is Bitter/Basic (Bleach/Maximum basic)**.
Remember **Exo = Exit** (heat exits/releases out), **Endo = Enter** (heat enters/absorbs in).

Use the sentence: **P**lease **S**end **C**harlie's **M**onkey **A**s **Z**ebra **I**n **L**ead **H**elps **C**opper **M**ercury **S**ilver **G**old (**P**otassium, **S**odium, **C**alcium, **M**agnesium, **A**luminium, **Z**inc, **I**ron, **L**ead, **H**ydrogen, **C**opper, **M**ercury, **S**ilver, **G**old).
Remember **Lavoisier** sounds like **Lavatory/Wash** — he washed away old alchemy myths and gave modern chemistry.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Oxidation and Reduction Agents
items.definition: Students often think an oxidizing agent gets oxidized. **Correction:** An oxidizing agent **gets reduced** while oxidizing other species.
Students think a higher pH means a stronger acid. **Correction:** A lower pH (closer to 0) indicates a **stronger acid**, whereas a higher pH (closer to 14) indicates a **stronger base**.
Students change chemical formulas (subscripts like $H_2O_2$ instead of $H_2O$) to balance equations. **Correction:** Only change **coefficients** in front of formulas, never the subscripts.
Students assume all salts have a pH of exactly 7. **Correction:** Salts formed from strong acid and weak base are acidic, and salts from weak acid and strong base are basic.

Students confuse heat sign in thermochemical equations. **Correction:** Endothermic reactions have a **positive (+)** enthalpy change ($\Delta H$), while exothermic reactions have a **negative (-)** enthalpy change.
A process where chemical bonds are broken and formed, resulting in entirely new substances called products.
Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products in any chemical reaction, formulated by **Antoine Lavoisier**.
Two or more reactants combine to form a single product ($A + B \rightarrow AB$). Example: Formation of slaked lime.
A single reactant breaks down into multiple products using heat, light, or electricity ($AB \rightarrow A + B$).
A reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its aqueous salt solution.
Mutual exchange of ions between two compounds, often forming a precipitate (precipitation reaction).
Addition of oxygen/electronegative element or removal of hydrogen/electropositive element; loss of electrons.
Addition of hydrogen/electropositive element or removal of oxygen/electronegative element; gain of electrons.
Acids release **$H^+$ ions** and turn blue litmus red; bases release **$OH^-$ ions** and turn red litmus blue.
Ranges from **0 to 14**; pH 7 is neutral, less than 7 is acidic, and greater than 7 is basic.
Reaction between an acid and a base producing salt and water ($Acid + Base \rightarrow Salt + Water$). tannin/indicators used.
Exothermic reactions **release heat**, whereas endothermic reactions **absorb heat** from the surroundings.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, focus heavily on direct identification of reaction types, color changes with litmus paper, and pH values of common substances like blood, lemon juice, and milk.
UPSSSC often sets traps by reversing the definitions of oxidizing and reducing agents. Always remember that the agent undergoing reduction is actually the oxidizing agent.
Memorize the reactivity series of metals using the provided mnemonic; questions regarding which metal displaces another from its salt solution are extremely common in PET exams.
Do not confuse the pH scale direction. Students frequently mark lower pH values as basic; always remember 0 is most acidic and 14 is most basic.

keyTakeaways: Chemical reactions involve breaking and making of chemical bonds obeying the Law of Conservation of Mass.
Redox reactions involve simultaneous oxidation (loss of electrons) and reduction (gain of electrons).
Acids turn blue litmus red with a pH < 7, while bases turn red litmus blue with a pH > 7.
The pH scale is logarithmic ranging from 0 to 14, where 7 represents neutrality.
Neutralization reactions between acids and bases always yield salt and water.
Reactivity series determines whether a displacement reaction will take place or not.
